name: Law of cosines
whenToUse: You know two sides and the included angle and want the third side, or all three sides and want an angle. On the AMC 10 it appears with $60^\circ$ and $120^\circ$ angles.
example: Sides $5$ and $8$ with $60^\circ$ between them: $c^2 = 25 + 64 - 2 \cdot 5 \cdot 8 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 49$, so $c = 7$. With $120^\circ$ instead, $c^2 = 89 + 40 = 129$.
pitfall: For an obtuse angle $\cos C$ is negative, so the last term is ADDED. When $C = 90^\circ$ it is just the Pythagorean theorem.
